The return is a delivery bet with a re-rating option, not a re-rating bet. At my fair multiple, the 14-month return of about 23 percent comes almost entirely from earnings growth and dividends. Earnings add 16 percent: the step from a flat FY2026 to FY2027 and FY2028, driven by the Transmission contract vintage and Electra, Republic Wire's full year, Grid capacity and falling interest. Dividends add 6 percent: a 2.7 percent yield growing about 10 percent a year. The multiple adds nothing, because on the model's EPS basis the stock already trades near the median.

The re-rating option is large but optional. Each 1.0x on the multiple is worth about 9.5 percent of return, and the span from the guideline floor (11.05x) to the stretch multiple (14.0x) is 28 points of return. Over 32 months, earnings contribute 27 percent and dividends 9 percent. The annualised return at the median, about 12 percent, is an ordinary compounding return; that is the honest description of a company whose EBITDA growth slows to 4 to 5 percent a year after 2028 without acquisitions.

A careful reader should make four adjustments to the tables.

  1. Basis: the multiple history is on brokers' EPS, which runs 6 to 9 percent above the model's basis, so every value in the tables carries a cushion of roughly that size; at the median multiple, the cushion takes the 14-month return towards +30 percent.
  2. Depreciation: my input change lowers the model's EPS by about €0.20 to €0.25 a year, which takes about 2 percent off each value.
  3. Capital deployment: the base case is a floor. €0.5bn to €1.3bn of acquisitions at 9 to 10x EBITDA by 2028 would add 4 to 10 percent to FY2028 EPS, and a buyback of the same size would add more; neither is in the model.
  4. Scenarios: in the downside case (FY2028 EBITDA about €930m and EPS about €8.6; FY2029 EPS about €9.4) at 11.05x, the December 2027 value is about €110, a total return of -3 percent. In the upside case (FY2028 EBITDA about €1,090m; FY2029 EPS about €11.8) at 14.0x, it is about €172, a total return of +51 percent.

Counter-case. The counter-case is the sector regime. With a beta of one, a further 15 percent de-rating of the electrification complex on capacity or interest rates would take the stock to the guideline floor whatever it reports, and the return to December 2027 would then be the +11 percent row at best. What would change my view of the return: the order plus an H1 2027 Transmission margin above 15.5 percent (move to the 14.0x row); a second acquisition at 10x EBITDA (lower both the EPS cushion and the multiple); a buyback (raise both).

Versus the market. The sell-side's mean target of €168 is the model's 15.82x row reached twelve months early. My central expectation is the €140 row plus the basis cushion: about €145 to €150 including dividends by end-2027, which is 15 percent below the street's targets and 25 to 30 percent above the current price.

Conclusion: At the Bottoming guideline of 11.05x the 14-month return is about +11 percent, and at my fair multiple of 12.3x it is about +23 percent (earnings +16, dividends +6, multiple flat); the model's +57 percent at 15.82x is a peak-delivery bull case. The return is therefore a delivery-and-dividend return, with a re-rating option worth about 9.5 percent per turn of the multiple.

Score: 77, set by the Rater. About +25% sits in the B band and maps to about 80; the return is led by earnings (+16) and dividends (+6), with the three-year check supportive. Moved down to 77 for the lower tail: a sector beta of one, an 11% return at the Bottoming guideline multiple, and a 5-8% correlated cluster taking the shares towards EUR 73 (-36%).

13Summary conclusion on the business and its investment case

Nexans is a good, focused industrial inside an excellent industry structure, and its earnings path to 2028 is more contracted, more mechanical and more predictable than its share price suggests. The stock's sector reputation and the company's own thin disclosure also understate that path. EBITDA rises from €805m to about €1,013m, and EPS rises about 26 percent in FY2027 and 19 percent in FY2028 from a flat FY2026. About two-thirds of the EBITDA increase rests on strengths already demonstrated; the undemonstrated third falls in 2028.

Nexans is, and will stay, the weakest of the three European high-voltage leaders. That position caps the Transmission margin at about 16.6 percent rather than peers' 20 percent, and it leaves a question mark over Halden after mid-2028. The compensations are European Grid, where Nexans leads and the street still under-models it, and a lower dependence on high voltage than NKT when supply-demand parity arrives around 2030.

The investment case over 12 to 24 months is an earnings-and-dividend return of about 20 to 30 percent at the stock's own median multiple. A re-rating option adds about 9.5 percent per turn of the multiple, and the sector regime will set the path.

The timing risk sits in one document and one margin print, and the sequence is fixed. The document is the replacement Halden order, probably signed by April 2027; the print is the H1 2027 Transmission margin in July 2027. February brings cuts to EPS and cash estimates, which the share price has absorbed and the brokers' models have not; July brings the proofs.

The skew is negative against consensus in the near term and positive against the share price, at roughly 2.5 to 1. The probability of guidance and sell-side upgrades is unusually low for the next event (February 2027) and close to even for the one after (July 2027).

The largest unpriced lever is capital allocation, and the board controls it. Management prefers acquisitions at 10x EBITDA to buybacks at about 7x, while the balance sheet deleverages to 0.5x net debt to EBITDA.

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 70, set by the Rater. Strong, funded external forces (72) and large dated internal moves (62) turn into a forecast EPS step of about 26% and 19% in FY2027-28 (B on topic 6, consensus EPS growth at the 86th percentile), with four-fifths of the FY2027 increase already contracted, acquired or mechanical, so the change surely reaches profits. It sits below Richard's Arteche 80 because the forces are offset (high-voltage award slowdown, European construction, input costs), the internal programme is unproven under a new team, and the profit step is front-loaded with a plateau after FY2028.

Foundations' Robustness: 60, set by the Rater. The industry is concentrated and disciplined in high voltage, Grid demand is framework-backed and regulated, and the guidance record has been clean since 2018 (topic 4 at 65). But Nexans is the weakest of three in high voltage, 40% of EBITDA follows construction with no pricing power, margins and cash are noisy, and the company's history (2013, 2018) is not stable or predictable (topic 3 at 57), so it sits above typical alongside Richard's Judges Scientific 60 rather than among the stable 80s.

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 60, set by the Rater. The case fits "cause-for-concern clearing in a medium-quality business, reverting to normal" in kind (identifiable, resolvable company items behind half the fall; a dated order and margin proof), but sits below Richard's 65-75 for CVS because the concern is modest against the business (Halden EUR 15-25m inside about EUR 900m of EBITDA) and today's problems blur the mechanism: a flat backlog with share loss, a Connect margin down 180bp, falling cash conversion and a stock whose moves are set mostly by its sector.

Case Riskiness: 55, set by the Rater. A simple operating case with a narrow EBITDA range, low fixed-rate leverage and a multiple low in its range (topic 9 at 56), but its equity outcome is less predictable than its operating lines: a dated binary on the order's timing, a new team after an unexplained departure, a 10x US acquisition exposed to a price war, a history of clustered execution crises and a share price that follows a theme-driven sector with a beta of one. That is the 50s level rather than Richard's paper-cut 80s.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
